about: The world map (OpenAI image generation through Codex CLI): the region from above, without lettering; pins and routes in source/world-map.json. Original in ~/Documents/living-tabletop-world-art/.

map.prompt:
Generate one image and save it as ember-crown--world-map.png in the current directory.

A world map for a tabletop role-playing campaign, landscape 3:2, seen straight from above like a hand-painted illustrated map (orthographic top-down view, no perspective, no horizon, no sky). A top-down illustrated map of a walled mining and forge town on a river crossing in a valley under low worn mountains, seen straight from above. A grey river runs along the bottom third, bending upward on the right. Stone walls ring the town. In the north wall, near the top centre, an arched gate between two square towers with a cart barricade behind it; above it, at the very top, an open grassy hill with a stone bench, campfires and a wooden catapult frame on its slope. Near the centre an upper terrace with a canopy, a long table and an old barn, broad steps running north to the gate. On the left a quarter of open work sheds with a glowing forge. In the upper right a battlemented wall over huddled coal-burners' houses, one tower cracked and smoking, grey-bannered tents on the field beyond it. On the right, above the river, market rows with cauldrons behind a river wall ending in a round water tower. At the bottom centre a small wicket gate and wooden pier, a low causeway threading left across reedy islets. Right of it a stone-arched bridge crosses the river; beyond, on the field near the bottom right, a white parley tent beside a banner tent. No people, no text.

Draw every place described above as a small, clearly recognisable landmark exactly at its stated position, with the roads, paths, corridors or waterways between them visible, so that markers can later be pinned on each landmark. Fill the whole picture edge to edge with the mapped land (no border, no frame, no cartouche, no legend, no compass rose, no scale bar, no grid). Absolutely no text, letters, numbers, labels or symbols that read as letters anywhere on the map. No people, no creatures, no figures.

The attached image is this campaign's cover: match its painting technique, palette, light and mood, but not its composition.

Match one consistent house style: original premium illustrated epic war fantasy for older teens and adults, muted painterly oil and gouache with confident ink lines and crisp readable silhouettes; the Ember Reach, a river valley under low worn mountains, and Ore Crown, a walled mining and forge city at a river crossing under siege: thick weathered stone walls and squat towers, pale ash lying like snow on the battlements and drifting in the air, black banners of the city's hundreds, each with a golden crown of embers, hanging along the wall walks, steep stone streets, workshop awnings and forge glow; beyond the walls a wide trampled field with distant camp fires, and catapults seen only as far-off dark silhouettes against the sky, never in detail; palette of ash grey and soot black, cold slate-blue morning light, weathered stone ochre, rust-brown iron and leather, banner gold, linen white and muted wool green, with warm ember orange and forge amber; grim hope in the ash, a tight defence, quiet courage and the weight of choices; every person shown is clearly an adult. Banners show only plain colour fields and simple emblem shapes; papers, plans, tablets and tokens carry only blank or illegible marks. No gore, no blood, no wounds, no corpses, no executions, no captives in chains, no threats to children, no anatomy, no weapons pointed at the viewer; no siege machinery details, no firearms, no cannons, no gunpowder. No franchise references, no anime look, no photorealism. No text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no border.
